executive_summary.headline: Three user-supplied Amazon links resolve to three verified air-fryer product pages. Prices, ratings, commission rates and trend data are not published, because they could not be verified or the Associates policy does not allow them on this site.
bullets: Re-verification (2026-11-14): each short link was resolved again; titles, breadcrumbs and also-viewed ASINs match the records. The Agreement's disclosure wording, the Participation Requirements text, the Conditions of Use licence and the FTC and Associates guidance were re-read. Corrections: policy section numbers (F-17), the 'Sponsored' label observations (F-10), and competitor labels marked as paraphrased (F-20). Brand bylines and specification tables were not re-read (F-18). The automation conflict with Program Policies is flagged (F-19).

Identity verified: each link resolves to an Amazon product page (ASINs B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH). All three sit under the same Amazon category path (Home & Kitchen > Kitchen & Dining > Small Appliances > Fryers > Air Fryers). Flag F-04 covers the short-link codes.

Pricing and ratings withheld: the Associates Participation Requirements (Section 2(b) and Section 6(t)) allow prices and star ratings on a site only through Amazon-served links or Creators API / PA API. The pages were read, but no price, rating or review count is published (F-02).
Commission potential not calculable: the category commission schedule is behind an Amazon sign-in, so no rate is entered (F-01). Third-party sources conflict on the Kitchen rate.
Attribution unverified: the resolved links contain no Associates tag parameter (F-03). Confirm the links are generated under your Associates ID before relying on any earnings.

Compliance: the required disclosure sentence appears on every page (R-01). Open legal items: the Conditions of Use limit collecting listing content, data mining and using Amazon content for AI models (F-11, F-12). The AI content automation is therefore NOT built.

Not built: automated product research, PA-API integration, click and conversion tracking, AI article generation and campaign optimisation. Each needs PA-API or Associates reporting access, a rate source, or a compliance decision first.
Site: static GitHub Pages site (source: main, path /; the root index.html redirects to docs/). Every table row links to an official source, and unverified values are blank and flagged.

Second verification pass (this session): all three link redirects, listing titles, category breadcrumbs, also-viewed ASINs and the absence of a tag parameter were re-read and re-confirmed; every policy quote on the site was checked against the live official page.

Three marketing drafts are now published as drafts: one article per product, a head-to-head comparison and a buying guide, with every sentence tied to a verified listing field and unclaimable statements listed separately.

Two new policy findings shape the design: Participation Requirements section 5 bars using Program Content to develop machine learning models (R-17), and section 6(y) bars price tracking or alerting on the Site (R-22), which limits the brief's pricing-analysis request.

Specification-table values (litre capacity, dimensions, colour, material) are carried forward from the earlier session's read rather than re-verified, because that table was not present in the page text this pass (F-18). A brand page for a similarly named model lists different dimensions (F-32).
Publishing the drafts still needs two things no environment here can supply: an approved Associates account with tagged links (F-31) and, for prices and ratings, PA-API or Creators API access (F-02).

buying_guide.meta_description: How to read an air fryer listing: basket count, capacity units, function names and the brand field, with the three listings on this site as worked examples.
buying_guide.intro: A guide to reading the listing, not a recommendation. It avoids performance claims, because those need proof the seller must supply (R-26), and it avoids prices, because this site may not show them (R-02).

decision_paths.question: Do you need two foods finished at the same time?
decision_paths.grounding: P1's listing title names two independent 3-quart baskets and Sync Finish, which is the only two-zone configuration in this set.

decision_paths.question: Do you need a single large basket instead of two small ones?
decision_paths.grounding: P3's listing title names one XL basket at 8 Qt with bake, dehydrate and frozen settings.

decision_paths.question: Do you need oven-style functions such as a rotisserie?
decision_paths.grounding: P2's listing title names 24 cooking functions, a dual-speed fan and a rotisserie in a French-door cavity.

decision_paths.question: Does the capacity unit match across the page?
decision_paths.grounding: On P1 the title says 6 Quart while the specification table says 6 litres, and on P2 the title says 26QT while the specification says 24.6 litres, so treat capacity as listed rather than comparable (F-06).

decision_paths.question: Is the brand stated plainly on the page?
decision_paths.grounding: P2's listing records the brand in Item details, while an earlier read of the page showed a different byline, so the brand field is worth checking on any listing before you repeat it (F-05).

platform.summary: The brief describes an AI platform. This repository is the data-driven research and content layer of that platform, built so that each stage can be automated only once its gate clears: a data source for research, a rate source for earnings, an account for links, and a compliance decision for automated generation. Nothing is faked to look automated.

guardrails: verify.py fails the build if any table row lacks an official-host link, so a source-free claim cannot ship.
verify.py fails if any price string or star-rating string appears on any page, enforcing R-02 and R-03 mechanically.
verify.py fails if the disclosure sentence is missing from any page, enforcing R-01.
verify.py fails if marketing copy claims a personal test or trial of a product, enforcing R-26.
External links are restricted to an allow-list of official hosts, so third-party stats cannot creep in.
The build is deterministic from data/*.json, and CI rebuilds it and diffs the result, so the published site always matches the reviewed data.
platform.scalability: Product records are data, so the site scales by rows: a new product adds one object to data/products.json and gains a table row, a verification block, a category entry and a content draft automatically. The scaling limit is verified data, not the site.
not_connected: Amazon Associates account or API keys

method: Start from the category Amazon assigns to the products, not from a guessed topic.
List the competing products Amazon itself shows beside each listing, and note whether that module is sponsored.
Score each candidate niche on demand, competition, ticket size, commission rate and content angle.
Leave an input blank when no official source supplies it, and record why on the Flagged page.
Re-score only when a data source changes, for example after PA-API access is granted.

reverification.method: Every product and policy value published on this site was re-read in a second, independent pass using automated retrieval of the official Amazon and FTC pages. A value is marked re-confirmed only if the same string appeared in this pass. Anything this pass could not reach is labelled 'carried forward' and flagged, never restated as verified.
